title: Microsoft 365 - Detected threats delivered through tenant or user allow overrides
subtitle: Defender XDR hunt for inbound messages with a threat verdict, explicit allow override and delivered outcome

deductions: The Q3 outcome statistics come from one Microsoft investigation; the schema and allowlist guidance verify field semantics but do not independently corroborate the campaign measurements.
The query is deliberately broad across threat verdicts, so necessary business exceptions and false-positive verdicts require tenant-specific ownership and prevalence review.
A safe positive control needs an isolated Defender for Office 365 tenant and a vendor-supported harmless simulation that actually populates ThreatTypes; the laboratory plan has not been executed.

decision: Publish as a Medium-confidence hunting query, not an alert. Investigate inbound messages for which Microsoft Defender recorded a threat verdict, an explicit organization- or user-level Allow override, and Delivered as the initial delivery action. Require policy ownership, current message state and interaction evidence before containment or promotion.
key_findings: Microsoft reported approximately 129 million malicious messages spoofing tracked business-service sender domains in Q3 2026; many were delivered after configured exceptions overrode protection. [C002]
In September, overrides applied to 63 percent of the studied messages with a recorded security outcome, with tenant-level overrides accounting for most of them. [C003]

EmailEvents exposes the threat verdict, organization/user override and delivery fields in one native schema; the hunt uses no IOC, threshold, join, body parsing or authentication-string assumption. [C004][C005][C006]

A match establishes only the recorded control outcome. It does not establish sender spoofing, failed authentication, user interaction, current inbox presence, compromise or a correct threat verdict. [C007][C009]
source_facts: Microsoft observed configured exceptions overriding protection for messages that failed authentication checks and were identified as malicious. [C002]
Microsoft's allowlist guide states that attackers exploit unnecessary allowlist gaps and provides the documented OrgLevelAction/ThreatTypes hunting primitive. [C004][C006]
The EmailEvents schema documents the fields and exact Delivered value used by the query. [C005]
analyst_assessment: Combining verdict, explicit Allow and delivered outcome is more actionable than auditing allow entries or threat verdicts separately because it identifies realized control bypass at message level. [C007][C008]
Latest delivery fields must be treated as enrichment because post-delivery remediation can change exposure after the initial Delivered action. [C009]
No ATT&CK technique is assigned because the generic control outcome does not establish a specific delivery or post-delivery attacker behavior. [C010]
assumptions: The target tenant has Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 and retains EmailEvents with populated organization- or user-level override fields. [C004][C005]
The literal Allow and Delivered values retain the documented semantics in the tenant and the advanced-hunting record represents the intended recipient/message event. [C005][C006]
Policy owners can distinguish necessary exceptions, test messages and false-positive verdicts during triage. [C008]
unknowns: The public research does not publish the affected tenants, individual policies, allow-entry scope or raw EmailEvents rows behind the aggregate override statistic.
The number of delivered messages that users opened, acted upon or converted into compromise is not established.
Target-tenant field completeness, benign prevalence, current-message-state reliability and policy ownership are unmeasured.
A vendor-supported harmless simulation that reproduces all four predicates has not been confirmed in the target environment.
technical_background: Microsoft's Q3 2026 email analysis found that attackers spoofed familiar business-service sender domains and that configured security exceptions could override malicious identification and failed authentication outcomes. An organization-level or mailbox-level allow entry can therefore convert a filtering verdict into delivery. Microsoft documents this decision surface in EmailEvents through ThreatTypes, OrgLevelAction, UserLevelAction and DeliveryAction. The query observes only the resulting control state: an inbound message with a non-empty threat verdict, an explicit Allow action and Delivered initial outcome. It does not parse AuthenticationDetails, infer why the exception existed, identify a brand, inspect message content or establish recipient action. [C002][C004][C005][C006][C007]

attack_chain.behavior: An attacker sends an inbound message; the Q3 study includes large-scale spoofing of familiar business-service sender domains.
attack_chain.observable: Sender and authentication fields are triage context only; the generic hunt does not require a particular brand or authentication result.

attack_chain.behavior: The Microsoft 365 filtering stack records malware, phishing or another threat verdict for the message.
attack_chain.observable: EmailEvents.ThreatTypes is non-empty, following the official override-analysis pattern.

attack_chain.behavior: An organization-level or user-level policy applies an explicit Allow action despite the threat verdict.
attack_chain.observable: OrgLevelAction or UserLevelAction equals Allow; associated policy fields identify the decision source for triage.

attack_chain.behavior: The service records Delivered as the initial delivery action for the recipient/message event.
attack_chain.observable: DeliveryAction equals Delivered; latest action and location are projected but not assumed to be unchanged.

attack_chain.behavior: Opening, click-through, credential entry, malware execution and compromise are possible downstream outcomes but were not established for each delivered message.
attack_chain.observable: Separate click, post-delivery, identity, endpoint and incident telemetry is required; the hunt does not represent this phase.

telemetry.purpose: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 processing records; requires the documented service prerequisite.
Limit results to inbound mail with a recorded filtering-stack threat verdict.
Establish that an explicit organization- or mailbox-level Allow action was recorded.
Establish the documented Delivered initial outcome.
Preserve a strong recipient/message pivot and event time for investigation.
Explain the policy source, verdict mechanism and authentication context without inferring their content.
Assess possible post-delivery remediation; these fields do not establish interaction.

telemetry.field: URL-click, post-delivery, sign-in and endpoint telemetry
telemetry.purpose: Determine whether the recipient interacted and whether any downstream compromise occurred.

query.logic: Select inbound EmailEvents rows with a non-empty threat verdict, explicit organization- or user-level Allow action and Delivered initial outcome.
query.match_proves: Defender recorded the threat verdict, explicit allow override and delivered initial action for the same recipient/message event.
query.match_does_not_prove: Correct verdict, failed authentication, sender spoofing, current inbox presence, recipient interaction, malware execution, account compromise or a specific ATT&CK technique.

triage: Preserve the raw EmailEvents row, query hash, Timestamp, NetworkMessageId and RecipientEmailAddress before policy or message remediation.
Open the message entity and establish which OrgLevelPolicy or UserLevelPolicy produced Allow; identify its owner, scope, justification, approval and expiry.
Review ThreatTypes, DetectionMethods and AuthenticationDetails as recorded data; do not assume failure or maliciousness from an empty or ambiguous value.
Compare initial and latest delivery fields and inspect EmailPostDeliveryEvents or Threat Explorer to determine whether ZAP or an analyst later moved or removed the message.
Correlate URL clicks, sign-ins, consent changes, endpoint activity and incidents for the recipient; absence of these layers leaves impact unknown.
Scope other messages sharing the policy, sender, cluster or message characteristics only after preserving the exact matched row and policy provenance.

false_positives.source: Necessary exception for a legitimate vendor or business workflow after a false-positive verdict
false_positives.control: Require a named policy owner, narrow scope, documented review, expiration and message-level provenance; do not silently suppress it in the query.

false_positives.source: Approved security simulation or mail-flow test
false_positives.control: Confirm the simulation identifier, test tenant or approved campaign record and verify that the exception is removed after testing.

false_positives.source: Stale or overly broad tenant/mailbox allow entry
false_positives.control: Treat as a control gap rather than a benign false positive; review scope, remove unnecessary entries and rerun the hunt.

false_positives.source: Threat verdict later corrected or message remediated post-delivery
false_positives.control: Use latest delivery state, post-delivery events and analyst disposition; retain the initial override as policy-risk evidence.

steps: Confirm Defender for Office 365 Plan 2, EmailEvents availability and population of all four predicates using raw historical rows without changing policy.
Measure 30 days of matches, resolve every policy owner and label necessary exceptions, simulations, false-positive verdicts and unexplained deliveries.
In an isolated non-production tenant, create a temporary narrowly scoped Allow entry and use only a Microsoft-supported harmless simulation that is first confirmed to populate ThreatTypes.
Run one allowed-threat positive and three negatives: allowed benign mail, detected-but-not-allowed mail and non-delivered detected mail; retain raw events and policy change records.
Remove the temporary exception, purge test messages, verify policy rollback and record any telemetry delay or missing field.
validation.success: The unmodified query returns the safe positive with all four predicates and policy context, excludes each negative for the intended reason, and historical matches have bounded, attributable overlap.
validation.rejection: Reject alert promotion if any required field is absent, simulation semantics differ from normal mail, necessary exceptions dominate without durable ownership, or current-message and policy context cannot be recovered.
visibility_gaps: EmailEvents requires Defender for Office 365 and documented licensing
Threat verdicts can be false positives or change after delivery
Latest-state fields do not prove that a recipient saw or acted on the message
The hunt does not cover undetected messages or exceptions not represented by the documented fields
validation.promotion_gate: Require retained safe controls, 30-day prevalence, complete field population, policy-owner accountability, bounded overlap, post-delivery triage and an approved response owner before designing alert logic.

conclusion: Fresh Microsoft telemetry shows that allow overrides can turn a threat verdict into message delivery at meaningful scale. EmailEvents provides a direct, documented and durable control-outcome hunt with no arbitrary threshold, but legitimate exceptions, false-positive verdicts and later remediation remain material. Keep the package at Medium-confidence hunting maturity until the isolated controls and tenant prevalence study are retained.
